gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 and Jackery Explorer 300D ship without a USB-C cable, or that a laptop needs a 5A e-marked cable to draw 100 W from any of these ports (an ordinary 3A cable stops at 60 W).
standout_why: I compared against The Gadgeteer's C300 DC review (cited) and the manuals.plus C300 DC guide (cited, but a PDF whose text I couldn't read). The Gadgeteer says Anker includes a '140 W USB C Charging cable' and reproduces Anker's port-sharing table, so the rivals partly cover the Anker. None of the rival pages, and not ChatGPT's answer, gives the 3A vs 5A cable rule. None says the BLUETTI or the Jackery 300D comes without a USB-C cable. ChatGPT's 300D card said 'Verify the exact USB-C port rating' and never gave one.
decides: This confirms the Anker SOLIX C300 DC as the pick that works at 100 W straight out of the box: its 140 W cable is included (per The Gadgeteer), and its 100 W and 140 W ports can run together. The Jackery 300D (140 W on each of two USB-C ports) and the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 (140 W + 100 W) can match it, but only after the buyer adds a 5A/100 W or 240 W cable. Otherwise a 3A cable they already own holds the laptop at 60 W. On the Anker, 100 W also holds only with up to three loads: with five loads Anker's table drops the 100 W port to 30 W.

findings.label: Cable needed for 100 W USB-C PD
findings.value: Above 3 A (that is, above 60 W at 20 V), 'a 5A wire with an E-Mark chip will be required'; 'many USB-PD charging cables sold individually in the market do not reach more than 60W'
findings.note: Cable maker's article. 100 W = 20 V × 5 A, so a 3 A cable stops at 20 V × 3 A = 60 W.

findings.label: What's in the box (US store)
findings.value: Elite 30 V2, AC charging cable, car charging cable, grounding screw, user manual; no USB-C cable listed
findings.note: Maker's US product page. The page states the USB-C port is 'PD 3.1 protocol, delivering up to 140W output'.

findings.label: Price, unit alone (BLUETTI US store)
findings.value: $289.99 (bundle with 60 W solar $399.99; with 100 W solar $489.99)
findings.note: Read from the product page. The URL is the 100 W-bundle variant; the page lists the unit-alone price separately.

findings.label: Accessory exclusions
findings.value: Does not support battery expansion with the B80, B300K or B230. A B80 can charge it in Power Bank Mode (sold separately).

findings.label: Weight
findings.note: Maker spec; just under the shopper's 10 lb limit

findings.label: USB-C ports
findings.value: Type-C1 and Type-C2: 140 W max each (5 V/9 V/12 V/15 V at 3 A; 20 V and 28 V at 5 A; PD 3.1, PPS). Type-C3: 65 W max (20 V at 3.25 A, PD 3.0). USB-A: 15 W.
findings.note: Maker FAQ spec table. It states no combined USB output cap. Only C1 and C2 reach 100 W; C3 stops at 65 W.

findings.label: What's in the box
findings.value: User manual and an AC charging cable (removable; doubles as the carrying handle); no USB-C cable listed

findings.label: Stated exclusions
findings.value: No 24 V car charging. Solar and car charging can't run together, nor can wall and solar. One solar panel only (two via an adapter not supported). No battery packs, parallel operation or car fast charging. Pass-through charging is supported.
findings.note: Maker FAQ. Weight given as 'around 2.5kg' (about 5.5 lb), listed as product weight.

findings.label: Cable in the box
findings.value: 140 W USB-C charging cable included; no solar (XT60) cable
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C300 DC Portable Power Station review (The Gadgeteer, 2024-11-26)
findings.note: Named reviewer's unboxing list. Anker's own product page did not list box contents.

findings.label: USB-C power sharing (Anker's manual table as reproduced)
findings.value: C1 100 W + C2/C3 140 W together. C1 100 W + C2/C3 140 W + USB-A 20 W with three loads. With five loads (C1+C2+C3+USB-A+car): 30 W + 60 W + 60 W + 20 W + 120 W. Total output 300 W.
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C300 DC Portable Power Station review (The Gadgeteer)
findings.note: So the 100 W laptop rate holds only with three or fewer loads. The Gadgeteer also reports a sticker on the box that cuts the car-socket rating from 120 W to 100 W.

findings.label: Ports and recharge (maker page)
findings.value: 2× USB-C 140 W PD 3.1, 1× USB-C 100 W, 1× USB-C 15 W, 2× USB-A 12 W, car socket 120 W; '7 Ports with 300W'; recharges at 280 W through two 140 W USB-C inputs
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C300 DC (Anker SOLIX US)
findings.note: Maker page. Recharging at 280 W needs two 140 W (240 W-rated) cables and two 140 W chargers.

findings.label: USB-C port
findings.value: One USB-C port: 5/9/12/15 V at 3 A, 20 V at 5 A, 100 W max; HUSB251 protocol chip (PPS, EPR PDO)
findings.note: Named reviewer's teardown quoting the spec. 100 W is only reached at 20 V × 5 A, so it needs a 5A e-marked cable. ChargerLAB gives the unit weight as 3.5 kg.
